doc.title: Toots Thielemans — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Jaco, honors, teaching and looking ahead
title: Jaco's decline and Brussels visit
summary: He recalls Jaco's last European tour and his Concorde trip to Brussels.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Unfortunately, you know, Jaco had a very, very tragic, tragic death.
Yeah.
Did you see him… did you see a kind of deterioration or anything like that?

No. No. Well, I saw him… I mean, when we played, when he was in Brussels for his probably last European tour, he went… after the show, he went. He had a… I don’t want to put, say anything that didn’t happen, but he did strange things, going to a beer place, a bar or a

café [unintelligible], and make noise and look to be… You know, apparently that’s what… But ‘til the last minute, I was Papa, you know. Of course. And he stayed even in Belgium became… when John Lennon died…
Yeah.
He had done that… song for John Lennon by John Lennon.
Imagine? No?
No.
A different one? Hmm. John Lennon died in December of 1980.

Well, he… you know, Jaco wanted to come to Brussels, and he came from wherever. Oh. He wanted… [laughs] That’s Jaco. He wanted… “Toots, you gotta come. I wanna see you to… I wanna… you gotta come and do your thing on the one track to Brussels and...” I was in Miami. “How do I get to Brussels?” I said. “There’s Miami–New York and New York–Brussels,” you know. [Regular?]. “No, I want to go with the Concord,” Mr. Pastorius. So we, he went to Miami to Washington, where he could catch a Concord, [if you please?]. And [laughs] from there, he got a Concord to Paris, and then from Paris he had to get… So… [laughs] And it costs… I don’t say. I don’t want to know. It’s not my business, but much more. And he was half a day later than if he had… you know? And we’re there waiting in Brussels, and he was… Come on, what’s the name of that John Lennon song? You’ll find it again.
Okay.
I can’t look here.
When we take the next break, I’ll look it up. Unless anybody in…

That’s Jaco. [laughs] And he stayed at our place and he came here, too. And he started to play with things. He started to throw these things, you know. It was [shuh?] [inaudible], you know. [laughs] That was some strong [stuff?].
Yeah.
But okay. But he was… it’s easy to say he was correct with the musicians, maybe, and not all that correct with his… dependence. I don’t know. It’s not [inaudible].
Again, it’s just a tragedy....
[inaudible/overlapping voices]
…a tragedy for such a genius to meet such a tragic fate.
Yeah.
